ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Citizenship: Historical, Cross-Cultural, and Interdisciplinary Perspectives. Description: This course takes an interdisciplinary approach to the history of citizenship, drawing the work of historians, social scientists, journalists, and writers. The first part of the course considers the history of citizenship, considering frameworks developed in antiquity and during the enlightenment, within empires and nation-states, and by twentieth-century social scientists. The second part applies these disciplinary and theoretical frameworks to special topics, including migration, race, gender, and the body, focusing on how these sites challenge and expand our understanding of citizenship.
